2217.unvetted: Edition question settled, contemporary-clear question not. Censimento (1964, Google Books seEYGFQqM1kC, old interface in Chrome) p. 48: its two Lorenzo pieces in 'BNF, GC, 137' are '[Niccolò Michelozzi] [3 lug. 1481?]' and '[Niccolò Michelozzi] 5 ago. 1481' (snippet images read); the Censimento gives no folios for GC 137, and Lettere V p. 262 (archive.org bwb_KU-999-230_5, search 'GC, 137') identifies the first as cc. 20r-21v, Lettere VI no. 509 p. 26 (bwb_KU-999-229_6) the second as cc. 6r-9r. The '137, c. 13' phrase hit on p. 48 could not be placed in any snippet and is not one of these entries; Lettere VI has no hit for Palavisino, Strasoldano or ghibellino. So no edition prints c. 13. Alignment test of c. 13r (BNCF0003827895, 985x217) against the clear strip c. 12r (BNCF0003827893, 1036x576, transcribed: 'El conte Girolamo ha sollecitato l'andata di m. Ascanio a Roma, qual si stima sia opera del S. L[odovi]co ... el palavisino ... m. Johanfrancesco ... el S. Lco et m. palavisino et strasoldano è sospecto assai parendo loro che lui sia di ghibellini', 261 letters): c. 13r transcribed to 263 tokens over 37 sign types (scratchpad c32/tools/align.py). Results: (1) the sign '11' occurs at least 8 times, so it is not the 'll' of sollecitato/ghibellini; (2) the near-repeat ('5 g 5 3 n m π 11 b t' end of line 1 / '5 y 5 3 n π b t' mid line 3) sits at about 22% and 61% of the strip, not where the two 'palavisino' fall in the clear (49%, 74%); it would fit 'el S. Lco et' (27%, 70%) better, but no consistent sign-to-letter table was found for it together with 'sollecitato'; (3) a beam-search crib alignment scored the c. 12r text no better than three unrelated Italian controls (cost 451 vs 451-525), i.e. no signal either way. The lengths (263 tokens vs 261 letters) and the opening code-like signs ('ħ y nō' for 'El conte Girolamo'?) keep the hypothesis alive. Needs a careful sign-by-sign transcription of c. 13r at higher resolution (the BNCF viewer serves 985 px only) and a proper homophonic crib attack; if it fits, verdict read (contemporary clear), if it is excluded, open.

2224.unvetted: Signs not printed in the edition. Chrome pass c32, Google Books NpzzAAAAMAAJ (TT 1906) old interface: '"titkos jel"' hits pp. 130, 131, 132 and one more; the p. 131 snippet shows the editor's placeholder in place of the sign ('a város szigségére és várára, az teb (titkos jel) kiről immáron ...'), p. 132 prints 'három ezer' in italics (in this series italics may mark enciphered words given resolved, as Teleki VIII p. 307 does). Lang 2015 repertory p. 248-249 C.Ker.01-04 'magyar jelek, megfejtetlen', részleges, and p. 68 n. 85 groups them with letters where only one or two words stayed unresolved. So the open part is one or two signs per letter and Komáromy did not reproduce them: the ciphertext is only in the originals (MNL OL E 185, Nádasdy family archive), not seen. Needs scans of the four originals (or their MNL online images if any) to see whether signs survive and whether anything is legible beyond the edition's placeholders.
